newsitem.title: JAPAN: Thailand calls for support from Japanese banks.
newsitem.headline: Thailand calls for support from Japanese banks.

text.p: Thai monetary authorities urged Japanese banks on Tuesday to continue their support for the country, saying that would be the key to restoring confidence in its beleaguered financial industry, bankers said.

Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and Central Bank Governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi met with representatives from 21 Japanese banks in Tokyo on Tuesday, a day after they secured $16 billion in loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Asian nations to rescue the Thai economy.

The two officials did not make any specific requests for new money or a rolling over of existing loans, but Japanese bankers took the Thai request for continued support to mean that they want existing loans to be rolled over, bankers said.

"The Thai finance minister and central bank governor asked us to continue the support that we have given them in the past," said the senior bank official, who attended the meeting but did not want to be identified.
Another bank official who attended the meeting said: "We generally had a positive impression about their attitudes towards regaining confidence over the nation."
"Unless the financial situation there gets worse, we are not planning to withdraw our money," he added.
Thailand's financial and economic crisis came to a head on July 2 when it decided to float the baht, setting off an attack by speculators which sent the value of its currency plunging.

The bank official said the Thai officials might have thought that the loan package worth $16 billion and a rolling-over of existing credits held by banks would be enough to overcome the current economic and financial crisis.
Thailand has nearly $89 billion in foreign currency debt, with Japanese banks accounting for nearly half of it.
The Thai officials also eased bankers' worries about the nation's bad loan problems.

They told the bankers they would protect creditors of the 42 Thai financial institutions that had their operations recently suspended amid sweeping measures taken by the government to restore confidence in the nation, bankers said.
"This is something new," said the first Japanese bank official.

The Bank of Thailand last week temporarily closed down more than half of the country's 91 finance companies, many of which were saddled with mounting non-performing loans extended to a collapsed property sector.
The Thai finance minister also urged Japanese firms and banks to not withdraw from Thailand, he added.
Thailand's financial sector has been hard hit by a liquidity crunch and rising non-performing loans due to over-exposure to non-productive industry, especially the property sector.
Some Japanese banks have exposure to those suspended finance firms, although the bulk of the Japanese money has been lent to subsidiaries of Japanese firms operating in Thailand.

An official at another Japanese major bank said: "It is still unclear whether the financial crisis there will come to an end, although the amount of the public assistance was larger than we had initially thought."
"The financial markets will probably make a judgment later," he added.
